Review.Independence: I reviewed the revision 3 contract, complete start-to-end diff, both cited rules, review 1, three run receipts and check logs, and the status and check reports. I wrote review 1. I did not author the change or its fixes and had not seen the authoring discussion.

Finding.Text: A declared trace's captured output could be mistaken for a later check's saved log when their filenames collided.
Finding.Resolution: Execution and recovery derive the same paths from the ordered selection. Where names could collide, each check receives a numbered directory. In run 3, TSLOW.output remained not-attempted while recovery saved TSLOW's captured output.

Finding.Text: A child surviving the runner could invalidate the recovered log's recorded hash by appending output.
Finding.Resolution: Recovery copies the bytes it hashes to a separate snapshot and publishes that path. Run 3 verified the receipt and snapshot after the surviving child appended to its original output.

Finding.Text: CK1 previously missed colliding log names and output written after the runner alone was killed.
Finding.Resolution: The fixture now selects TSLOW and TSLOW.output, kills the runner alone, and releases the surviving writer after receipt publication. Assertions check both verdicts, the changed original and the unchanged snapshot bytes and digest.

Finding.Text: Recovery could report a missing header while the live runner was publishing it.
Finding.Resolution: The runner takes the adjacent SQLite lock before creating its log directory. Recovery tests that lock before looking for the header. CK1 verifies the live diagnostic while ownership is held and refusal after release when the header is still absent.

Review.Adequacy: Run 3 executed the recovery cases on Windows. They exercise identity retention across amendment, distinct check ownership, trace-log preference and output fallback, missing artifacts, hash stability after a surviving writer appends, concurrent and repeated adoption, live ownership, malformed and missing headers, non-counting status and the first required check preventing closure. The POSIX-only graceful-signal case was skipped.
Review.Rule: The exclusive reservation and atomic publication preserve existing receipts. Recovery retains original identity and definitions, records adoption time, identifies attempted checks from their own artifacts and records hashes of stable log snapshots. Neither recovered verdict counts.
L-36 records the motivating lost run, the alternative, costs including snapshot storage, and the observable condition for retiring explicit recovery.
